original_title: Polynomial compatibility on the Boolean cube from disjoint-support separators
abstract: We give an explicit affirmative answer to the two-polynomial question posed by Austrin in Oberwolfach Report 9/2025. Two nonzero real multilinear polynomials of degree at most d on the uniform Boolean cube have a common nonzero vertex whenever every relative coordinate influence is at most 1/(4096d⁸). In fact, disjoint supports force a relative influence at least 1/(1024d⁸). The result is a deduction from the disjoint-support separator of Li–Li–Li–Liu and the covariance inequality of O’Donnell–Saks–Schramm–Servedio, combined with a square-density estimate. We supply the complete deduction and an explicit separator constant. No novelty or first-priority claim is made for this consequence.

claim.domain: All positive integers n,d; nonzero real multilinear f,g of degree at most d on the independent uniform sign cube
claim.normalization: Full squared L2 norm includes the constant Fourier coefficient
claim.separator: Prior total deterministic tree, T <= 16 d^4, no repeated branch queries
claim.covariance: Prior real OSSS inequality, with independent coordinate resampling and factor 1/2
